topicName: Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) and Always Encrypted
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Technical Tutorial: Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) and Always Encrypted in Microsoft SQL Server"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Data protection is a paramount concern for enterprise database administrators. Microsoft SQL Server provides two robust features for data security at rest: Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) and Always Encrypted. While both protect your data, they serve distinct architectural purposes and operate at different layers of the database engine."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"1. Transparent Data Encryption (TDE)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"TDE performs real-time I/O encryption and decryption of the database, associated backups, and transaction log files without requiring modifications to the application. It protects data at rest (storage level) against offline attacks, such as someone stealing physical hard drives or backup tapes."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"How TDE Works"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"TDE uses a symmetric key called the Database Encryption Key (DEK). The DEK is secured by a certificate stored in the master database, which in turn is protected by the Service Master Key or an Extensible Key Management (EKM) module."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing TDE (Code Example)"},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"-- Step 1: Create a Master Key
USE master;
GO
CREATE MASTER KEY ENCRYPTION BY PASSWORD = 'StrongMasterKeyPassword123!';
GO

-- Step 2: Create a Certificate protected by the Master Key
CREATE CERTIFICATE TDECertificate WITH SUBJECT = 'TDE Protection Certificate';
GO

-- Step 3: Switch to your target database and create the Database Encryption Key
USE MySecureDB;
GO
CREATE DATABASE ENCRYPTION KEY
WITH ALGORITHM = AES_256
ENCRYPTION BY SERVER CERTIFICATE TDECertificate;
GO

-- Step 4: Enable TDE on the database
ALTER DATABASE MySecureDB SET ENCRYPTION ON;
GO"},{"order":9,"type":"heading","text":"2. Always Encrypted"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Always Encrypted is designed to protect sensitive data, such as credit card numbers or national identification numbers, stored in SQL Server databases. Unlike TDE, Always Encrypted allows clients to encrypt sensitive data inside client applications and never reveals the encryption keys to the Database Engine."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Components of Always Encrypted"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Column Master Key (CMK): A key protection key that protects one or more column encryption keys, typically stored in an external key store like Windows Certificate Store or Azure Key Vault."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Column Encryption Key (CEK): A symmetric key used to encrypt data in a specific database column."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing Always Encrypted (Code Example)"},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"-- Creating a table with an Always Encrypted column using deterministic encryption
CREATE TABLE Employees (
    EmployeeID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    SSN VARCHAR(11) CIPHERTEXT 
        ENCRYPTION BY DEFAULT 
        WITH (ALGORITHM = 'AEAD_AES_256_CBC_HMAC_SHA_256', 
              COLUMN_ENCRYPTION_KEY = MyCEK, 
              ENCRYPTION_TYPE = DETERMINISTIC)
);
GO"},{"order":16,"type":"heading","text":"3. TDE vs. Always Encrypted: Summary of Differences"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Protection Scope: TDE protects entire databases at rest on disk. Always Encrypted protects specific columns, safeguarding data even while in transit and in memory from DBAs and compromised database servers."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Application Changes: TDE requires zero application code changes. Always Encrypted requires connection string adjustments and client-side driver support."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Threat Vector: TDE protects against physical theft of media. Always Encrypted protects against malicious DBAs, compromised host servers, and insider threats."}]
